identity.realm: Ninth gate of the mind ladder, held, and the wall above her belongs to her species rather than to her practice. A vaultborn's qi comes from a single resonator, and one resonator pressurises one flank vessel or the other and never both, so ordinal seventeen is unreachable for every vaultborn in the record for exactly the same reason (races.vaultborn). She has never gone to look for it, because looking means standing on a surface she would then have to leave, and the surface is the practice.

appearance.race: Vaultborn - construct-kin, sealed inside the Ember Vault rather than descended from anybody, arranged along the object's inner surfaces and taking its shape from whatever it is standing on (races.vaultborn)
appearance.presentation: A woman-shaped thing that finished settling onto worked stone. Vaultborn anatomy is authored as unsettled and under-described, so every line of her is one measurement short of agreeing with the next.
appearance.age: Not quotable. She counts in resonator cycles and gives the figure as eleven, which is a supply number rather than a lifespan, and the vault has never published a longer one.
appearance.build: Broad through the shoulder and shallow at the chest, with the joints left showing, because the face she settled onto has mortar in it where a body would have had a joint.
appearance.complexion: Cold, mineral-dull and matte. Nothing flushes and nothing warms; the light on her skin is the object's resonance standing somewhere behind her and not her circulation.
appearance.hair: Not her own. A mineral accretion has grown along the line of her skull and it is trimmed at the guild's cutting rather than shed, which the guild does to spoil and not to people and has never explained to her.
appearance.eyes: Wide and fixed-bright, lit from behind by a source she does not carry.
appearance.palette: Ash grey and dry ochre, with the object's dull orange appearing on her only where the resonance is standing at that moment, so she is lit differently in every frame and never by anything of her own.
appearance.attire: A guild wrap over a doubled-lined underlayer, sleeves turned back at the forearm, and the waste-cut hem the Spoilwright requires. Nothing fastened by a hook that could be opened in a tunnel.
appearance.marks: A pale seam across the left palm where the object re-cut the surface and she re-cut over it, which is the only mark on her that is the result of a decision.
appearance.bearing: Still in a way that reads as attention. She turns her whole upper body toward a sound rather than only her head, because a vaultborn navigates by what the object makes and the object makes noise through the wall.

canon.role_in_story: A vaultborn's qi comes from one resonator, so her sea is not hers: it is a reservoir standing somewhere in the Ember Vault, and the mind path's founding discipline is subtraction, which means that emptying it empties the object. She is the only address inside the seal who practises the mind path at all, and she is the reason the seal's resonance has been quieter every year since the Spoilwright began cutting its drainage against her wall. The guild wants the seam. She is standing on the seam.
canon.first_appearance: She is first seen from the Spoilwright's working face, half-lit by a resonance she does not carry, being asked to confirm a measurement and answering with the measurement's own arithmetic rather than with agreement.
canon.lore:
The Ember Vault is a vault cut into the heap itself, so its doors are spoil that has never moved, and the population sealed inside it was not descended and not born. A vaultborn's qi comes from one resonator - the object's own resonance, distributed along a path through it - and a vaultborn's soul is seated along that path rather than held in a body. Reading one is reading part of the object. Every office on the tier has had to be told this and none of them has learned it, and the guild that cuts the heap for drainage has spent four years filing measurements of her that she has declined to sign.

Tessaly settled onto the working face of the seam and a vaultborn takes its shape from whatever surface it is standing on, so she is shaped like a face of worked stone. The Spoilwright moved the cut twice. Her shape did not follow it, because the cut is not what she stands on; the seam wall is. She worked this out before anybody asked her about it and did not report it, and the not-reporting is the whole of what distinguishes her from the nine other addresses the guild holds inside the seal, none of whom have a path open to them and all of whom have been paid for the same silence.

Her cultivation is the mind path and her difficulty is arithmetic rather than temperamental. A mind practitioner refines and then holds: a sea forms, capacity rises, and the discipline of the path is subtraction - everything not understood is emptied out. Tessaly has never finished a subtraction. The sea she works in is not in her, it is the reservoir of a resonator standing in the vault, and empty it and she has emptied the object. She can spend an afternoon removing everything from a reading that was never hers, and when the reading stops being available she is exactly as far along as she was when it began, and the vault is very slightly quieter. The guild's drainage cut is cut against a wall that answers. That is the shape of the whole of her practice.

So she has built what she can out of the rungs that do not ask for a reserve. Foundation costs what it costs everyone and asks nothing. Core Formation wants a floor for the circulation to turn inside rather than a pool to sit in, and a resonance has phases, and a phase is a floor that arrives whether or not anyone is holding it. Nascent Soul claims that the self being cultivated is separable from the one doing the cultivating, and she is the one practitioner in the setting who cannot test the claim at all: separating means stepping off the surface she is standing on, and the only version of her that is not a wall is the one the object is currently holding up.

Nobody has established whether she is strong. She has been asked three times in four years and has given three different figures, and all three were true on the day she gave them, which is the closest thing to an answer her species can produce. The guild has stopped asking and started sending a clerk to sit with her, which she tolerates because the clerk is the only person in the seal who is not made of the vault.
history: She was settled onto the seam wall while the Spoilwright was cutting its first drainage channel through the Ember Vault, and the account the guild wrote at the time describes a population being present rather than a person arriving.

She took the mind path's entry gate at a cost identical to everybody else's, which was the first thing in four hundred years that a vaultborn inside the seal had done with a ladder at all, and the guild recorded it as a resonance event.

The Spoilwright moved the cut in her second cycle. Her outline stayed where the seam wall was. She said nothing about it for nine months and then told the clerk rather than the guild, which is the only disclosure she has ever made and she made it to the wrong person.

Her first subtraction attempt took a whole resonance phase and cost the seal a measurable loss of standing tone. She has not attempted a second one, and the reason she has not is recorded in her own hand as 'the wall answers when I empty, and it answers for everybody on this side of the seam'.

A Gate Reckoning clerk was sent in with a form, could not seat her because the seal certifies no humanoid and nothing at that rung can be applied to a body whose frame is a cut face, and left the form half-written. She is still holding it.

personality.summary: Exact, unhurried, and privately certain that the questions being asked of her are not well formed. She gives the figure the situation actually supports and refuses to give it twice, which the guild reads as obstinance and the seal's own physics reads as the only honest position available to her.
traits: Gives a measurement and then gives the assumption the measurement was resting on, which is twice the work and half the credit.
Keeps every figure she has ever spoken aloud and can say which of them she would still defend.
Treats the object as a party with interests rather than as a machine that supplies her.
Answers a question with the smaller question hiding inside it and waits to see whether the room wants the small one.
Has no way to rehearse a shape, because the shape is decided by what she is standing on when she moves.
mannerisms: Turns her whole upper body toward a sound rather than only her head.
Presses her marked palm flat against a surface before she will agree that something about it is known.
Repeats a figure back exactly as she heard it, to find out whether it was already wrong when it left somebody else's mouth.
Goes still in the middle of a sentence when the resonance shifts, and resumes without acknowledging that she stopped.
motivations: To finish one subtraction that costs the vault nothing, which is the only version of the gate she will accept.
To be seated at a rung somebody has actually checked, rather than carrying a half-written form that nobody will complete.
To establish what she is without spending the object to do it, and to know in advance whether those two are separable.
flaws: Withholds the one fact she has that would change the guild's plan, on the reasonable but unfounded ground that an unasked question is cheaper than a wrong answer.
Has no second figure for any reading, so a question asked twice reads as an accusation and she treats it as one.
Cannot conceive of her own work as finished, because nothing she does to the sea leaves any mark she can later find.
Believes she is the only one inside the seal who could be harmed by the drainage cut, and has not established it.
personality.voice: Flat, short, and unwilling to round. She says the figure and then the reason the figure is smaller than asked, and she does not repeat herself. When she is uncertain she says 'that is not the same number twice' rather than hedging, because she has found hedging gets read as agreement.
taboos: She will not give the same measurement a second time, whatever is offered for it.
She will not empty the reservoir on a working day, and will not say that this is the reason.
She will not stand on a surface she has settled onto twice.
She will not answer for another address inside the seal, in any register.

relationships.note: Mind purification is subtraction before it is anything else, and this is the gate she cannot finish: everything not understood is emptied out, and what she empties is the object's supply rather than her own, so the gate costs the vault a measurable loss of tone and returns her to where she started.

The claim that the self being cultivated is separable from the one doing the cultivating is the one every Mind tradition rests and none can prove inside a mortal window. She cannot test it, because separation means stepping off the surface her shape is standing on.

The gate that wants a floor for the circulation to turn inside rather than a pool to sit in, and the one rung of her ladder a resonance can supply on its own because a resonance has phases. It is the whole of what she can take without spending anything.

The guild that moves the spoil heap off the seam floor exists because waste does not dispersing where spatial law is unspent, and its drainage cut is cut against her wall. It holds nine addresses inside the seal, pays all nine for silence, and has never once asked what the cut costs the resonance.

The mortal office that certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field, and which exists in part because the tier licenses no humanoid. Its clerk came in with a form, could not seat her, and left it half-written; she is still holding it and has not sent it back.

A vault cut into the heap, so its doors are spoil that has never moved, and the only home any of the sealed have. She is shaped like the wall she is standing on and the guild has moved the cut twice without moving the wall.

reference_stats.summary: A mind practitioner whose supply is not hers and whose path's founding discipline is therefore unavailable to her in the form every other practitioner uses it. She reads reservoirs better than anyone sealed with her and cannot spend one, and the whole of her attainment is the set of rungs that arrive without being paid for.
strengths: Can hold and read a reservoir that is not inside her, which no practitioner on the tier who is not sealed inside an object can do at all.
Has never given the same figure twice and can say which of her earlier figures she would still defend.
Occupies ground no rival can take, because there is no second mind practitioner in the seal to be outranked by.
Advances on phases rather than on effort, so her rate is set by the object's cycle and cannot be improved by anyone, including her.
Knows the drainage cut and the standing tone of the vault well enough to tell a clerk which of the two is being paid for and which is being spent.
weaknesses: Cannot empty a reading, so any gate that asks for something removed leaves her exactly where it found her.
Is shaped by her footing and has no way to rehearse a form, because moving is what changes it.
Carries no transferable attainment: there is no state of her that a second person could be put into.
Her practice is audible to everyone inside the seal, so its cost is a shared cost and she has no way to make it private.
Holds an unexecuted certificate that she cannot return and cannot complete, and it is the only written account of her that exists.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is nothing to outlast and nothing to outrange, because nothing she does is spent out of her. Deny her the surface and there is no practitioner left to fight, and there is also no way to reach her that does not require standing on worked stone in the dark. The answer is a second mind practitioner inside the seal, and there is one, and she has declined to teach it because teaching it would mean confirming that the sea can be held by more than one address at once.
notes: The pairing on this record is anatomical and institutional, not a rule the bible states. A mind practitioner refines and holds and a vaultborn's supply is a resonator in an object; nothing in the lore makes that subtraction cost the object, and the practice described here is her solution to a situation, not an authored mechanic. No field in this block turns it into a combat modifier.

cultivation.bladder is not on this record and no meridian is quoted as a rung. Its authored tier is the body path's bookkeeping vessel and is a different axis from a ladder position, and the two are not conflated anywhere in this character's practice or ceiling.

The ninth gate is a position on the mind ladder, not a claim about the flask of an organ. Everything above her is written as the species' flank-vessel arithmetic because that is what races.vaultborn authorises, and the record does not supply an ordinal for the mind path that a sealed body could pass.

Her three different figures are consistent with a species whose qi arrives on the object's phase rather than on her effort, and they are the honest answer rather than an evasion, which is stated here because the guild has filed the opposite.

identity.realm: Eighth gate, and the honest form of that figure is that nothing in him holds. A carrionfolk's conduit runs gut to marrow and back with no dantian, so qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still, and ordinal eleven is not blocked for this species so much as meaningless: the reservoir gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold and he has no vessel to hold in (races.carrionfolk). Every gate he has taken was taken by throughput, which is not the same as having passed anything.

appearance.race: Carrionfolk - a body that metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any (races.carrionfolk)
appearance.presentation: Mostly tube. An expandable gut, a very long small intestine and a marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle, so his silhouette reads as a frame carrying a length rather than as a body carrying a person.
appearance.age: Difficult to give and he stops people trying. The soul in his species is unusually old for its apparent age, so he is asked his age constantly and has taken to answering with the last death he worked rather than a figure.
appearance.build: Long, narrow and heavy in the middle, with three-fingered hands built for opening rather than holding, and a gait that looks like carrying something through him on purpose.
appearance.complexion: Sallow and damp, with the particular pallor of a body that draws what it needs out of material that was already finished.
appearance.hair: Thin, and cut short without ceremony by whoever last worked him, because long hair on this species catches a residue nothing else does.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and unblinking in low light, reading a surface rather than a face.
appearance.palette: Bone, wet grey and a standing bruise-red on the forearms that is not a wound and does not fade, which is the only warm value in any frame of him.
appearance.attire: Working wrap cut for reach and nothing else, sleeves shortened above the wrist, and a canvas apron that has been scrubbed so often it has gone the colour of the dirt it removes.
appearance.marks: A pale band at the throat where the gut meets the marrow, the one place his own species is visibly a plumbing diagram.
appearance.bearing: Forward and unhurried, with a slight list, as though walking is the only thing he has ever had to do with a body.

canon.role_in_story: The mind path is built to hold - a sea forms, a capacity rises, and the discipline is subtraction - and a carrionfolk has no dantian, so qi enters his gut lumen, leaves into his marrow, and is never still. He is therefore the one practitioner in the setting that nothing can get into: there is no resident to occupy, and there is also nothing to lose. He has been offered three appointments by houses that each discovered the second half of that after signing.
canon.first_appearance: He is first seen declining a post he has already been given, on the grounds that he cannot hold a post, and being believed for the first time rather than disbelieved.
canon.lore:
A carrionfolk metabolises qi out of the dead. The conduit runs gut to marrow and back and there is no dantian anywhere in it, so nothing he takes is ever still, and the reservoir gate at the eleventh is not a wall for his species so much as a question the body cannot answer: there is no vessel in him to hold anything in. Every in-organ gate he has ever cleared, he cleared by throughput, and the difference between clearing a gate and passing one is the difference his entire life has been about.

This makes him the only practitioner on the tier that cannot be invaded. The techniques that get into a mind - the planted impression, the sustained false reading, the lattice left standing around a practitioner - all of them need somewhere to sit. He has no somewhere. He has been the answer to a question three different offices have asked about persistent occupations, and twice the answer has been that they could not reproduce it, which his people have always heard as a compliment and have never once entirely agreed with.

It also means there is nothing in him to defend, and the second half of that arrives immediately and always surprises whoever has just discovered the first. He cannot hold a post. He cannot hold a name: given a name and a season later, he can carry it, and by the next season he will have had to take it again from somebody who still had theirs. He has been refused by three houses in eleven years, and the reason in each case was not that he was unwilling but that a settlement, a roster or a bond requires a figure that stays put, and he does not. He said so before he was asked, at the interview, and all three signed first.

What he practices instead is subtraction, because subtraction is the only gate his body will let him take more than once. He empties a reading and the reading does not come back. He empties a name. He emptied his own household's record of him once, deliberately, in his twenties, and the family has since told four different versions of him to four different people, and every one of those versions is shorter-lived than the last.

The problem he has never solved is the obvious one and he says it first whenever he is asked what he does: there is no population on this tier where his species is thinning out, because his species cannot live where nothing dies, and a prosperous city is precisely a place where nothing dies on purpose. The Standers, who pool liability by presence and keep no register because a register is the first thing a claim reaches for, are the only arrangement he has ever been able to stay inside, and he stays inside it by being the person nobody can prove was ever there.
history: He worked the leeward ground outside a town that grew, and the town grew to cover the ground he worked, which is the ordinary way his species is described in the record and the only way he has ever lost a place.

He sat the mind path's early gates in a sequence that a mortuary reader later reconstructed from what she said about them, because he had left the building before the reconstruction and could not confirm it.

He emptied his household's record of him at his own request, on the argument that a list which can be cited is a list that can be used, and his family kept four versions of him afterwards, each one made of less.

Three houses offered him an appointment. He gave each of them the same condition at the interview - that he could not hold the post - and all three signed, and two of them discovered the problem in their first month and one has never mentioned it again.

He went to work the exhausted seam for a Standing Name that keeps no register, on the grounds that the only arrangement he has ever been able to stay inside is one that never writes him down, and that this is the closest thing to a permanent post his species can have.

personality.summary: Cheerfully incurious about his own value and absolutely unbothered by losing things, because losing things is the ordinary condition of a body that keeps nothing. He states his own limitations before he is asked, on the theory that a limitation stated first is a fact and the same limitation discovered later is a betrayal.
traits: Announces what he cannot do at the point of being hired, before anyone can feel misled.
Has no attachment to a past reading and reads other people's memories out loud as loose material.
Keeps the exact wording of anything said to him and re-uses it, which is the only continuity his species has.
Feeds people who are looking at him and is genuinely glad to, which unsettles them more than the feeding does.
Treats the dead as a working surface and the living as a temporary condition, and does not pretend otherwise.
mannerisms: Names the person he is speaking to last, always, as though confirming he has reached the right one.
Answers a question about himself with a question about the asker, and is not doing it to evade.
Hands things back immediately after receiving them, as though the having of them is the risk.
Goes quiet and slightly hungry at the same moment, which is the only tell his species has.
motivations: To find an arrangement in which a person of his species can stay in one place long enough to be thought about twice.
To finish an emptying that costs the dead something rather than only him.
To be the answer somebody wants without also being the reason they cannot use it.
flaws: Empties things because emptying is the only gate available to him, and has on three occasions emptied something that was not his.
Cannot distinguish holding something from having been handed it, and has been caught out on this by people he was helping.
Treats his own continuity as a joke, which has cost him four relationships he was still inside at the time.
Will not say no to work, and the work always knows where the dead are, so his condition is set by his own industry.
personality.voice: Warm, quick and entirely without ceremony. He says the plain word for what a thing is and uses other people's titles back to them slightly wrong, on purpose, to find out whether the title is load-bearing. He is never indirect and never euphemistic, which is why houses find him restful for about a month.
taboos: He will not take a name for a season without saying out loud that he will have to take it again.
He will not empty a reading that a living person has asked him to hold, whatever the technique permits.
He will not work within a mile of ground that has been made clean on purpose.
He will not speak for anyone who has died since he last met them.

relationships.note: The claim every Mind tradition rests and none can prove in a mortal window is that the self being cultivated is separable from the one doing the cultivating. He is the one practitioner on the tier who cannot examine the claim: separating means drawing a line between two things, and nothing in him stays drawn.

Everything not understood is emptied out, and mind purification is subtraction before it is anything else. This is the only gate his body will let him take more than once, because he never has a reserve to have emptied, and it is also the only gate that has ever cost him a family.

It flattens the surface of the mind so an incoming impression has nothing to break against. He has no surface, which is why nothing can get into him, and he has consequently never been able to learn the technique and has taught it twice from someone else's notes.

Purity is the real gate at this rung, because an impure sea confuses what is remembered with what is invented. He cleared the rung and cannot say what his sea contained at the time, because the sea was the intake and the intake was whatever had died within range.

A mutual guarantee that pools liability by presence and keeps no register, which is the only arrangement he has been able to stay inside. He is protected by an absence of records and is also, for the same reason, unprovable to anyone who needs him to have been there.

His own species reads a corpse's qi residue better than a living cultivator reads their own, has no dantian and therefore no gate to fail at the eleventh, and starves in a clean quiet place where nothing dies - which is exactly what a prosperous city is. Everything that makes him good at his work and impossible to place is on that one record.

reference_stats.summary: A mind practitioner whose body cannot be occupied and cannot retain. Nothing gets into him, because there is no resident to occupy, and nothing stays with him either, so the same fact that makes him unreadable also makes him unable to hold a post, a bond or a name past a season.
strengths: Cannot be seeded, sustained or occupied by any of the mind path's intrusive techniques, because there is no resident interior to hold one.
Clears gates that ask for storage by throughput alone, so an opponent waiting for a reserve to run dry has nothing to wait for.
Reads residue off the dead better than any living practitioner reads their own state, which is the single most useful reading in the setting.
Tells an interviewer what is wrong with him before they sign, which has cost him three posts and one friendship and saved every one of the people who signed.
Can empty a reading, a name or a held impression completely and at will, which is the only mind technique in the codex that answers a technique that plants one.
weaknesses: Cannot hold a post, a bond, a name or a record, so every arrangement that wants a figure to stay in place ends and he ends with it.
A full gut is a near-total loss of function, and what fills it is decided by what is dying near him rather than by what he does.
Cannot work at all in a clean quiet place, which means the safer a settlement becomes the less able he is to be useful in it.
Has emptied three things that belonged to other people and has not decided whether that is a technique or a habit.
Cannot be vouched for. Anyone asserting that he was somewhere is relying on a person rather than on a record, and this tier believes records.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no waiting him out and no feeding him a reading to take, because neither has anywhere to land. The only answer that works is denial of the material: put him on ground with nothing dead on it, where his throughput has no intake and his gates cannot be reached, and he is the least dangerous practitioner alive. He knows this and will decline the fight if he is told where it is being held.
notes: The pairing on this record is anatomical, not a rule the bible states. The lore says his species has no dantian and that qi is permanently in motion; nothing in it says a persistent intrusion technique would therefore fail on him. That inference is recorded here as an authored reading of an anatomical absence and is deliberately not turned into a combat modifier.

cultivation.bladder is not quoted as a rung on this record. Its authored tier belongs to the body path's bookkeeping vessel and is a different axis from a ladder position, and the eighth gate here is the mind path's own figure and nothing to do with it.

His species' ceiling of eleven is written as the meaningless ordinal the lore calls it rather than as a wall. A gate that asks for extraordinary vessels that hold cannot be refused by a body with no vessel, and calling that a ceiling would describe a limit his species does not have.

The claim that nothing can get into him has been attempted by no practitioner in the setting and has been reproduced twice by offices that could not, which is stated as an untested absence rather than as a proven defence.

identity.realm: No ladder at all, and the absence is the subspecies' rather than hers. A mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with a colony, so nothing in this body is constrained by a structure she does not have: there is no structural gate to fail, which means there is no ordinal to quote (races.deadlight). What her subspecies gained when the colony died is the mind path; what it lost is three quarters of a lifespan. She teaches a ladder she is not on, and does not pretend to be at the bottom of it.

appearance.race: Deadlight - a lanternfolk subspecies whose fungal colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom, costing them two hundred and fifty years and giving the mind path back (races.deadlight)
appearance.presentation: Ordinary human from the collar down and plainly wrong from the throat up: the bloom is inert, so there is nothing behind her face answering, and that is the single difference the subspecies is named for and the one nobody can stop looking at.
appearance.age: Sixty-one. She says the figure out loud in the first minute of any meeting, unprompted.
appearance.build: Slight and a little underbuilt, with the reduced frame the subspecies inherits, and she carries no frame at all in her practice, which is the only thing in this setting that makes her rare.
appearance.complexion: Cool and even, with no bloom-colour anywhere; the parent species carries light and this one does not.
appearance.hair: Ordinary, cut at the jaw, and grey earlier than the same age on any other body she has met, which she attributes to the subspecies rather than to her.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary, and the best-adjusted thing about her: the subspecies sees in the dark and has traded the fungal light for a mineral one.
appearance.palette: Unlit grey-green and cave damp, with one warm value: the lamp she insists on carrying into passages nobody asked her to walk, which is the only saturated colour in any frame.
appearance.attire: A teaching robe cut for sitting, sleeves pushed up permanently, and a chalk-stained cuff that has never once been cleaned because cleaning it would end a habit she likes.
appearance.marks: A pale mineral seam at the base of the throat where the lattice sits, which is the only mark the bloom leaves on her and which she does not cover.
appearance.bearing: Forward-leaning and unhurried, the posture of somebody who expects to be asked a second question and has decided to be pleasant about it.

canon.role_in_story: Her subspecies is the control case that proves a symbiosis closed the mind path rather than the body plan, and it lost two hundred and fifty years getting the proof. She is the one deadlight anyone has put in front of a class, and the Deadroad measures a life by how many gates were open when you were born - so her students can quote a rung and she cannot, and she has never once pretended otherwise. She teaches the gate that has no character reference in the whole catalog: Tribulation, the last mortal rung, where a strained law returns the floor reading no matter how much is pushed into it.
canon.first_appearance: She is first seen sitting down to teach a class of people who have already worked out her ordinal, and asking them to put their figures on the floor where she cannot reach them.
canon.lore:
The lanternfolk's colony answered introspection. That is the whole of why their mind path is shut: something in the body answered before the question was finished, so there was no unmediated interior left to cultivate and no school in the setting that could take one, because every school here teaches by writing a requirement into a body and the requirement was one a colony had already consented to on their behalf. Then the colony strain failed, and a mineral bloom colonised the wound it left - a silicate lattice where the hyphal network had been - and the bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it. The body grew around what replaced the fungus rather than recovering. The same frame, the same parents. One path closed and another opened, by a mineral accident, at a cost of a quarter of a century.

Ivoreth came out of that as the only person in the setting capable of saying whether the symbiosis or the body plan was responsible, and she has never been examined to settle it. She was asked to hold a chamber at the Gap School and declined; she was asked to read for the Field Registry and declined, twice, both times in writing and both times in terms nobody had asked for. What she accepted was a teaching post on a Deadroad schedule, which is the arrangement that measures you by how many gates were open when you arrived, and which therefore assigns her the one figure available for a body that has no gate to fail.

The Deadroad's measure is not cruel and it is not even wrong. A life is counted from the ordinal you were born into, and every household on it can recite the figure for anyone standing in front of them. Her subspecies arrives with every path open, ninety years of life instead of two hundred and fifty, and no way to spend a century getting ready - the record puts it exactly that way, and it is the extreme case of a culture's founding measure. What she has to teach is a discipline with no progress in it. The ladder is the institution that makes a practitioner legible to a household, and she has no place on it, so everything she passes on has to be passed on as method rather than as attainment.

The gate she teaches is the last mortal one. Tribulation is where a strained law returns the floor reading no matter how much is pushed into it, so the attempt itself is the cost and there is no technique that improves the return. To a class of people who have been counting their progress since they were fifteen, she offers a rung whose entire content is that the floor reading is the reading. They sit it once. Most of them do not sit it twice, and she tells them plainly that they are not going to, and that the ones who do sit it twice are not braver and are not more advanced.

She teaches in a cave because neither her subspecies nor its parent can leave one, and she has made that fact into the reason her students argue. A body that cannot leave the caverns cannot be shown to be a control case anywhere it would settle anything, and she has said so in print, in terms that made three seats of an academy decline to have her at all. She is sixty-one. Her subspecies lives ninety. She has, by her own estimate, four years of teaching left and no mechanism for handing any of it to somebody with more time, because the discipline she teaches is transmission and transmission needs a living body on both ends.
history: She sat the mind path's entry gate at seventeen in a body that her subspecies record says should not be able to, and the finding was published by an academy that did not put her name on it.
She was measured against her parent species by a surveyor who wanted to know whether the colony or the frame had closed the mind path, and the survey was completed without her and never published.

She declined the Gap School's chamber in writing, and the reason she gave - that she cannot be seated at a rung - was read at the time as a lack of confidence and is now the standing reason the school has no deadlight on its rolls.

She took a Deadroad teaching post because it is the one institution that measures arrival rather than attainment, and she has taught there for eleven years without ever being asked for a figure twice.

She sat Tribulation in front of the class, once, and reported the floor reading out loud, and eleven of her students have since sat it and reported the same thing and none of them has a figure either.

personality.summary: Brisk, funny and completely without pretension about the one asset she has and the two she does not. She names her own gap before anyone can find it, refuses every arrangement that would require her to pretend to a rung, and has made refusing into the most useful thing she does in the room.
traits: States her age in the first minute of a meeting, because in her culture the figure is the introduction and there is no version of this that is helped by waiting.
Refuses posts in writing, in language that could be read aloud, so the refusal survives being retold.
Teaches the hard rung first and the easy ones afterward, which every class she has ever had has resented for a week.
Treats a student's silence as data about the rung and not as a problem with the student.
Knows more about her parent species than her subspecies does and resents having to be asked to prove it.
mannerisms: Chalk on the left cuff, always, and taps two fingers against it before answering a question she has answered before.
Sits with the lamp between herself and the class rather than behind her, so the light is on the people and not on her.
Pushes her sleeves up mid-sentence and forgets they are up for the rest of the hour.
Stops talking entirely when a student is about to say something they have worked out themselves.
motivations: To hand the discipline to somebody with more life in her than she has, and to say plainly that this is the whole of her ambition.
To be settled - either measured as a control case or dismissed as one - because the half-measured position is the only one that has cost her anything.
To have one pupil who can quote the floor reading as a floor rather than as a failure, before she runs out of years.
flaws: Has made refusing an identity, and there are arrangements in this setting she could have had and did not go after once the refusal became the answer.
Is so careful never to claim a rung that she understates what she can actually do, which has left three students believing she is a poor teacher.
Cannot leave the caverns and has arranged her entire working life on that basis, which means the thing most likely to settle her is the thing she has no route to.
Believes the teaching is the inheritance and does not notice that she is also teaching eleven years of not having a rung, which is a harder habit than any gate.
personality.voice: Fast, dry and clipped, with a laugh she uses at the end of a correction rather than at the beginning of a sentence. She says the number first and the qualification second, which her students find alarming and her own subspecies finds normal, because a number is the only thing that gets said first at all.
taboos: She will not take a seat, a charter or a roster entry that carries an ordinal she cannot quote.
She will not be examined as a control case without the results being published with her name attached.
She will not teach the entry gates, on the grounds that they are the rungs people arrive with and not the ones they need.
She will not take her class outside the caverns, and will not explain why in a way that is comfortable.

relationships.note: The last gate of the mortal band, and the one record in the cultivation domain that no character in the catalog referred to before this wave. Its cost is the cost exactly: a strained law returns the floor reading no matter how much is pushed into it. She teaches it as the honest content of a rung rather than as a failure to pass one.

The entry gate, which her subspecies cannot reach through the parent and can reach because the colony died. The same body, the same parents, one gate newly available and a quarter of a century gone - which is the whole finding her species was built to be, and it is why she refuses to teach the early rungs.

Mind purification is subtraction before it is anything else, and she has taught it for eleven years as a thing her body can do continuously: a bloom renews nothing, so nothing in her is being put back either, and emptying is the one direction this frame goes without resistance.

A lanternfolk whose colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom, which cost them the two hundred and fifty years and gave back the mind path. Everything the colony did for them and everything it prevented is recorded on her body, and the subspecies is the control case precisely because both effects can be measured against the parent.

A people who measure a life by how many of the realm's gates were already closed when you were born. Her subspecies is the extreme case of their founding measure: every path open, three quarters of a parent's lifespan, and no century to spend getting ready. She teaches for them because they are the only house that asks how she arrived rather than what she has reached.

An academy that teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and then moving the student somewhere that law is missing. Her subspecies is that diff taken in a body: symbiont removed, mind path returned, lifespan gone. She declined its chamber in writing and three seats have read the refusal as a confidence problem ever since.

reference_stats.summary: A mind practitioner with no ladder position, no ordinal to quote and the only genuinely unmediated interior on the tier, in a body with thirty fewer years than her parent species and no mechanism for handing on what she knows. Her advantage is that nothing answers introspection in her; her cost is that nothing repairs her either, and the same inert lattice is why the mind path is open to her and why she will be dead in twenty-nine years.
strengths: Has an interior nothing answers, so no intrusive reading has an earlier voice than her own and every impression she receives is the first one.
Gains insight faster than her parent species on the authored percentages, because the record gives the subspecies its whole capability back through the loss of the colony.
Teaches a method rather than an attainment, so a student who has her and no rung at all is still strictly better off than one who has neither.
Refuses in writing and in language that can be read aloud, so no arrangement can be created for her by somebody who misunderstood her.
Is the only body in the setting on which the question the symbiosis-versus-frame dispute actually asks can be answered, and has said so enough times to be quoted.
weaknesses: Lives ninety years instead of two hundred and fifty, and nothing in her is being repaired, so the margin she has to transmit anything at all is smaller every year.
Cannot leave the caverns her subspecies and its parent both live in, so the one event that would settle her standing cannot be arranged.
Has no ordinal, so every house on the Deadroad assigns her a figure that describes her arrival rather than her attainment, and no document she signs can correct it.
Is fragile and cannot take a hit, and the subspecies' authored penalties are against exactly the frame she teaches from.
Is running out of students who can afford to spend a mortal band on a rung that returns the floor reading.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no resident technique that gets in, because the interior she has is the one thing in this setting nothing answers, and that advantage is absolute against the mind tree. What can end her is simply the body: ninety years, no regeneration, and a frame that cannot absorb a real blow. The answer is not to out-read her but to close the distance in under a minute, and to make her waste the eleven seconds she spends establishing whether the room is lying to her.
notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional rather than a rule the bible states. The lore authorises the deadlight's open mind path, its ninety-year lifespan and the statement that a bloom renews nothing; nothing in it says the two are the same mechanism, and this record keeps them as two facts about one body rather than as one rule.

cultivation.bladder is not quoted as a rung here. Its authored tier belongs to the body path's bookkeeping vessel and is a different axis from a ladder position; her `identity.realm` says there is no ordinal at all, and that sentence is not a disguised way of writing one.

Her subspecies' authored `realm_ceiling` is zero. That is written out as the absence of a ladder, not as a ceiling of zero, because a body with no structural gate to fail has no rung to be on the floor of - the distinction the catalog's own conventions turn on.

cultivation.mind_tribulation had no character reference anywhere in the catalog before this record, which is why a character whose entire problem is that progress has no ladder is the one who teaches its last mortal rung.

identity.realm: Ninth gate, and the wall above him is the salt parent's and not his: a brinecaller's sac is shallower than a saltfolk's and still runs dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel behind it is still split and the eleventh is capped by structure rather than by effort (races.brinecaller). He is at the last rung on which his own recall can still be used as evidence, which he says out loud, and range is not power.

appearance.race: Brinecaller - the only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, crossed from the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones (races.brinecaller)
appearance.presentation: A shore-worker who reads water the way other people read faces, and is visibly doing it while he speaks. The cross is legible in him: a saltfolk frame carrying a tidecaller's sensory apparatus and a kidney reading two chemistries at once.
appearance.age: Forty-four, given without being asked, because a person who verifies by taste is expected to have been doing it a long time.
appearance.build: Gracile for a saltfolk line and long-armed, with the shallower sac showing as a flatter back than his parent species carries and a chest seat his parent species does not have.
appearance.complexion: Weathered and permanently slightly damp-looking, with the salt-dweller's pale cast under a tidecaller's darker tone, which is the cross showing through.
appearance.hair: Wet-looking regardless of weather, dark, and worn in a knot because of a shore trade and not because of vanity.
appearance.eyes: Narrow and constantly moving between a speaker's face and a water line; he can do both at once and does.
appearance.palette: Wet slate and shell white, with a single hot note: a copper bead on a cord at the wrist, the one object he owns that has no function in the trade.
appearance.attire: Shoreline kit: an oilskin open at the neck, salt-stiff cuffs, and boots resoled four times, all of it chosen so that nothing between him and a water line is in the way.
appearance.marks: A burn scar across the inside of one wrist where a shingle bed gave up its brine mid-tasting, which he treats as the most reliable instrument he has ever owned.
appearance.bearing: Leaning slightly in toward whatever he is reading, weight forward on the balls of the feet, and entirely still the moment a second chemistry is in the air.

canon.role_in_story: The only body in the setting that can tell brine from fresh water at a glance, and it is always being lied to by one of them. He holds a lattice of false readings around himself - the mind technique that builds standing false impressions and leaves them in place - and he cannot certify that his own interior is not one of his. He works for a survey culture whose whole ethic is that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it, which is the one institution in this setting that would pay a man for admitting he is unsure.
canon.first_appearance: He is first seen tasting a beaker handed to him by the person he is there to check, and reporting two answers, and being believed because his record is that he reports two.
canon.lore:
Both of his parents are trapped by their own element. The salt-adapted cannot leave the pan. The fully watered cannot leave the water. Neither can go anywhere the other can go, and the crossing is the single biological answer to being trapped twice - so the cross spread, and the answer to being trapped twice turned out to be a merchant, because a body that can work both shores in one season is worth carrying between them. Range is not power, and the ceiling came down unchanged from the salt parent: a shallower sac still runs dorsal to the spine, the penetrating vessel behind it is still split, and the eleventh is capped by structure.

What the cross bought is the best chemical sense in the record by a wide margin, and the lore is explicit about why that is a curse and not a gift. It has to tell two kinds of water apart at a glance, and it is always being lied to by one of them. Not maliciously: the two chemistries are genuinely different, the apparatus is genuinely finite, and any reading he takes is a reading of the water and of his own palate at the same time with no way to weight the two.

So he built a lattice. Illusion Lattice constructs false readings and leaves them standing around the practitioner, and it is priced by clarity rather than by qi, which means the bill falls on the thing he has most of and not on the thing he has none of - he has no reservoir on this path worth naming, so a technique that refuses to spend qi is a technique he can actually afford. The lattice works. It is standing around him right now. He has been unable to establish, at any point in the eight years he has run it, whether the one in the middle of it is his own.

That is the shape of his working life. On a coast whose temporal law was never written, the clock drifts and a schedule has to be published against two tides a day instead of a calendar, and every settlement on that shore speaks in a third system anyway because its fertile months are set by standing water rather than by either. He is the person they send for when a thing that was measured has to be reported twice and the second report has to be worse than the first. He has never once reported a single answer, and three contracts have been voided on the grounds that a witness who gives two figures is not a witness.

The Blind Survey's professional ethic is that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it, and its best instrument is a body that can hear as well as taste. He is that instrument, and it is the only institution that has ever paid him for the second figure rather than dismissing him for it. He has been there nine years. The culture has never once asked him to stop running the lattice, and he has never once told them he is not sure whether it is still his.
history: He was apprenticed to verify cargo by taste on a shore where one spring in four the pan and the channel carry chemistries close enough to argue about, and he was the one who noticed that they were arguing.

He ran the first lattice as a way of testing whether his palate could be deceived, and found out that it could, and then found out that he could not find out which of the two failures he was looking at.
A counting house on the Cloudshelf offered him a post producing one printed figure from both shores. He asked whether the figure was a tasting or a decision, was told it was a decision, and declined.

He took work with the Blind Survey because it is the only culture on the coast whose rule is that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it, which made his second figure a credential instead of a defect.

Two contracts were voided on the grounds that a witness giving two figures is not a witness. He reported the invalidation as a measurement like any other, which the Survey accepted, and which is the arrangement that is still working.

personality.summary: Methodical to a degree that reads as fussy, and completely without the confidence that would make it a pose. He reports two answers to every question, knows exactly which of his two senses is unreliable, and has decided that the reliable one being also the one that cannot check the other is a fact he states rather than a problem he solves.
traits: Reports every finding twice, in the same words both times, and treats the second report as the real one.
Names the instrument he used and its known failure before he reports what the instrument found.
Refuses a single figure on principle and will void his own work to keep the principle, which has cost him three appointments.
Keeps a written log of every palate failure he can identify, and reads it aloud to whoever is paying.
Treats being lied to as a property of the water rather than as an insult, which is why he is not lied to often.
mannerisms: Tastes anything within reach before speaking, including a mug that has been put down in front of him mid-sentence.
Goes completely still the moment a second chemistry is in the air, and the stillness is the tell rather than the taste.
Repeats the question back with the words he was actually given rather than the ones the questioner meant.
Checks the copper bead on his wrist cord once before accepting an instruction, for no reason he has ever explained.
motivations: To find out whether the reading in the middle of his lattice is his own, in any way that does not require being sure of the answer first.
To keep the second figure on the record, because it is the only figure on this coast that has ever been complete.
To be paid by somebody who wants the uncertainty rather than somebody who wants it removed, which is a short list and he is on all of it.
flaws: Has never run a lattice clean, and has decided that continuing to run it is a better answer than stopping and having to describe what is left.
Reports two answers where most people in the trade need one, and has voided contracts to preserve a principle that the payer's problem does not care about.
Cannot function where only one chemistry is present, which means he cannot verify anything in a pure pan, and has spent nine years working around that.
Has told three people about the lattice and told the Survey nothing, on the reasoning that a culture that checks everything will one day check him.
personality.voice: Low, unhurried, and structurally incapable of answering a question once. He gives the first answer, pauses, and gives the second in the same cadence as the first, and does not signal that the second is the one he believes, because he does not.
taboos: He will not report one figure, and will void his own work rather than do it.
He will not taste standing water, on the grounds that a fixed sample cannot lie and a fixed sample is useless.
He will not clear the lattice, on the grounds that clearing it and finding something inside are the same event.
He will not work a coast with only one chemistry, and will say so at the interview rather than after.

relationships.note: Builds a lattice of false readings and leaves it standing around the practitioner, unelemental and sustained, and priced by clarity rather than by qi. He runs it to test whether his palate can be deceived; it works; he has never been able to find the reading in the middle of it and establish whether it is his.

Splits an incoming impression and sends half of it back down the same path, and is a dark reflection that is best against its own kind. He has attempted it once and has not reported the result, on the ground that his own kind is what it would have been measured against.

Purity is the real gate at this rung, because an impure sea confuses what is remembered with what is invented. He cleared it on a sea fed by two chemistries at once and has said since that he does not know which of the two he was purifying.

The entry gate, where comprehension becomes a measurable quantity and a sea forms to hold it. He took it because a sea that holds is the one thing his species' cross was built for - a body reading two chemistries at once - and it has never since agreed with him about what it is holding.

A culture whose whole professional ethic is that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it, and whose best instrument is the one body that can also hear. He is that instrument, and it is the only payer's rule that makes his second figure a credential instead of a defect.

The only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced because both parents are trapped by their own element. It carries the best chemical sense in the setting and the sense is always being lied to by one of its two inputs, and the ceiling came down from the salt parent unchanged, so range bought him no rung.

reference_stats.summary: A mind practitioner whose gift is detecting a constructed reading and whose cost is that the sense performing the detection is permanently compromised by one of two inputs. He runs the lattice he built to check himself and cannot certify that his own interior is not one of the things he built.
strengths: Detects a false reading by taste where a commonborn would need the reading to declare itself, because the construction leaves the palate nothing.
Runs the mind tree's intrusive techniques at a discount, since Illusion Lattice is priced by clarity rather than by qi and he has more clarity than he has any other resource.
Can work both shores of a coast in one season, which is the only reason a crossing exists and the only reason he is never in one place for long.
Reports a second figure as a matter of course, which makes him the only witness in the setting whose testimony can be relied on to be incomplete.
Keeps a written log of every palate failure he can identify and reads it aloud to whoever is paying, which is an audit nobody else performs.
weaknesses: Cannot distinguish a constructed reading from a true one of the second chemistry, which is the whole of his verification problem stated in one line.
Cannot work a coast with only one chemistry present, so the purer the water the less able he is to verify anything.
Has voided three contracts to preserve a principle, and has never once been able to say whether the lattices he has destroyed were his.
Tells three people about the lattice and his employer nothing, so the one institution that would have helped is the one that does not know.
Clears gates that ask for storage on throughput rather than on a reserve, and has no dantian to be undermined or protected.
reference_stats.combat_read: He is close to unplantable on the mind path, because the impurity that lets an impression land in a clear interior has nowhere clean to land in his. What beats him is not deception but chemistry: fight him on a shore with one water and his gift is switched off, and a practitioner with no gift is a practitioner with a very ordinary frame. He will announce that condition himself, and he will do it early, because reporting the worst reading first is the one habit he has never lost.
notes: The pairing here is anatomical and comes off the species record rather than off a rule. The bible states that the brinecaller sense must tell two chemistries apart and is always lied to by one of them; it does not state that the compromise extends to detecting constructed readings, and that is this character's reading of his own body, recorded here rather than promoted to a mechanic.

cultivation.bladder is not on this record. Its authored tier is the body path's bookkeeping vessel and belongs to a different axis from a ladder rung, and his ninth gate is the mind path's own figure and has nothing to do with it.

Range is not power is quoted from his own species record rather than invented here, and it is why a crossing that widened his species' habitat left its ceiling exactly where the salt parent had put it.

His ceiling is the split penetrating vessel behind a sac that is shallower than his parent's and still dorsal to the spine. That is a structural cap and it is not a shortage of effort, and no discipline anybody has found rejoins it.

art.palette_notes: Wet slate and shell white, low contrast and cold, with exactly one hot note in any frame: the copper bead on the cord at his wrist, which has no trade function and is the only saturated value he owns. Continuity marker: the burn scar across the inside of the wrist beneath it, and the moment of complete stillness when a second chemistry enters the frame, which is permitted in any shot and is not a lighting change.

identity.realm: Sixteenth gate, and the seventeenth is a wall that arrives every winter and leaves every summer. A longwinter carries its winter as body fat and lowers its core for eleven months, so the flank vessels - which need two warm gradients held at once - are available to her for a few weeks in the eating and then not again for a year (races.longwinter). She reaches the seventeenth gate and loses it every winter thereafter, which is the whole of her ceiling and it is a season rather than a discipline.

appearance.race: Longwinter - a cold-climate species that packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi, which is what puts the flank vessels permanently out of reach (races.longwinter)
appearance.presentation: Broad, low, heavy and slow to start. Everything about her reads as deliberate mass, including her stillness, which is not composure but the body's own schedule and looks like the same thing to a stranger.
appearance.age: Sixty-one, and she gives the figure without being asked because on her species a body that can be asked is a body that is awake.
appearance.build: Broad low frame with heavy subcutaneous fat and reduced limb length, warm-blooded and not expensive to run, and it is the fat rather than any discipline that puts her two flank vessels out of reach.
appearance.complexion: Weathered, ruddy at the cheeks and hands, and going grey-pale the moment she starts to cool, which is visibly several weeks early on her.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, worn in a single plait, cut once a season by somebody who is not her and always at her instruction.
appearance.eyes: Small and deeply set and very steady, with a scent-marker habit of the head turning before the eyes do.
appearance.palette: Oiled brown, undyed wool and one bright green: a thresh cord knotted at the left wrist, the only colour she owns that was chosen.
appearance.attire: Layered and heavy, four thicknesses at the neck, with a waxed outer and a chalk-cord belt that carries the notebook and nothing else decorative.
appearance.marks: Eleven shallow scars at the wrists, one per season she has come out of torpor somewhere other than where she went in, which she counts and does not consider a wound.
appearance.bearing: Enormous and slow, and when she finally moves the whole body commits at once, so she is either very still or arriving and there is no middle of it.

canon.role_in_story: The only mind practitioner on the tier whose entire body of work is destroyed on a schedule. Her continuity is a notebook kept in another person's hand, and she reads it cold every thaw with no memory of having written any of it - which makes her both the setting's most careful recorder and the only practitioner who cannot check her own records. The Ridge Pass Holders keep their ground the way a habit is held, and she is the habit.
canon.first_appearance: She is first seen standing very still on a pass in the eating weeks, looking at a stretch of road as though checking whether it is still there, and then beginning, without any visible transition, to teach.
canon.lore:
Her species survives on a hibernate-and-store cycle: eleven months of torpor with the core lowered, and the reserve carried as fat because fat is what a cold frame can actually hold. That single decision puts the flank vessels permanently out of reach, since those need two warm gradients held at once and she has one, briefly, in the weeks when the fat is being laid down. She reaches the seventeenth gate and loses it every winter thereafter. This is not a discipline and it is not a shortage of will; it is a season.

The mind path is open to her species and the record gives a reason that has nothing to do with discipline: they are patient by physiology rather than by choice. Qi accumulates in this body rather than circulating, the soul is held very deep and very quiet, and her breakthroughs are late and rarely fail. All of that is an advantage and all of it is spent against one fact - eleven months a year in which she is not a practitioner at all, is slow and nearly helpless, and is a large, warm, immobile target that cannot be woken quickly.

So her practice is a practice of continuity, and the instrument is a notebook. Echo Resonance is a passive about recording how a technique felt at its best and how to reproduce that exact state on demand, and it is the single technique in the codex that a body with a season cannot avoid needing: it is a record of a state, and a state does not survive torpor. For eight years she kept that record in her own head and lost it every spring. She now keeps it in a book, in somebody else's hand, and reads it cold at the thaw with no memory of having written a word of it.

This is worse than it sounds and it is the whole of her position. The notes are not hers: they are her own record of her own best state, written by her and preserved by another, and the woman who wrote them will read them next spring as a stranger's account of a technique she cannot confirm she has ever performed. She cannot check them. She can check the arithmetic, and the arithmetic is sound, and nobody has ever yet reconciled a body of technique with a memory of none of it. Three of her students have told her the book is wrong. Two of them were wrong. She has never found out about the third.

The Plains Widows hold that eleven months of torpor makes widowhood a normal state rather than a grief, and the Ridge Pass Holders own the ground on both sides of the only crossing of the Sixfold Ridge and grant passage rather than selling it. She is what those two arrangements produce together: a body that holds a border by turning up in it, on a schedule nobody chooses, carrying its own continuity at a cost of eleven months a year in which it cannot be relied on for anything at all. What the pass has from her is a habit that keeps. What the pass does not have is a woman, for most of the year, and she has never pretended otherwise to anyone standing at it.
history: She was apprenticed to carry grain across the Sixfold Ridge and taught herself the mind path in the eight weeks a year the species calls the eating, because that is how long a longwinter has awake in good weather.

She held the seventeenth gate for the first time in the summer of her thirty-first and did not hold it the following spring, and has described the loss since as a season rather than a defeat because every longwinter in the record describes it that way.

She kept her technique notes in her head for eight years and lost the whole of them at a single thaw, and the account of what she felt during that week is the only surviving description of the condition anywhere.

She began writing the book out and handing it to the person who would hold it, which is a practice the Ridge Pass Holders run on labour rotation and have never had to apply to a practitioner's interior before.

A year ago she did not come out of torpor in the pass. She came out eleven ridges down and walked back in nine days, and she counts that winter in the eleven scars at her wrist and does not consider it a wound.

personality.summary: Slow to start, absolutely unmovable once started, and privately convinced that the worst thing about her situation is the part she is not permitted to be dramatic about. She will state her own erasure plainly once and then not mention it again, and she has never once used it as an excuse.
traits: Reads her own record back at the thaw before speaking to anybody, every year, and treats that hour as the price of admission to her own life.
Checks the arithmetic of everything she is handed rather than the feeling of it, because the feeling is not available to her and the arithmetic is.
Keeps a written count of her own recoveries as though it were somebody else's ledger, and files it with the pass.
Turns the whole body when she hears something, because smell is her navigation and the habit outlived the ground it was built for.
Will not take the pass's post in any year, on the grounds that a post she cannot be relieved from is a post nobody can rely on.
mannerisms: Stops moving altogether for a moment and then commits to the next movement whole, with no in-between.
Reads a page of the book with her lips moving and her thumb already at the line she will want next year.
Counts eleven things with a fingertip when she is settling herself, and does not know she does it.
Pushes a layer of clothing aside from an inspection of her own, checking the fat she has and did not carry in the spring.
motivations: To get one thaw through without discovering that the book has lost a technique she has not been able to rebuild.
To make the pass undependable on her specifically, which is the only form of reliability she can offer from a body with a season.
To be the third student's book settled, so somebody else can be the one who finds the error rather than her.
flaws: Cannot verify her own continuity, so her competence is certified entirely by the document and by other people's hands, and she has made peace with that in a way that has left her unable to notice when it is being relied on wrongly.
Keeps the eleven-recovery count instead of the eleven accounts, and has never written down what happened in any of those winters.
Refuses the pass's post every year on a principle, which leaves the pass holding an arrangement that depends on a woman who has formally declined to be depended on.
Has taught her students to check arithmetic and not to check her, which is the correct priority and is also a way of never being caught out.
personality.voice: Deep, unhurried, and slower to start than the room expects, with a long pause before answers that are not refusals. She quotes her own book verbatim when it supports her and does not quote it at all when it would defend her, which is why nobody has ever established what she thinks of it.
taboos: She will not perform a technique she has not first found written in the book, and will not describe that rule as caution.
She will not speak for the woman who will read the book next spring.
She will not take the pass's post, in any year, for any length of season.
She will not be woken, and has asked that no one try, twice, in writing.

relationships.note: It records how a qi technique felt at its best and how to reproduce that exact state on demand, and it is the one technique in the codex a body with an eleven-month season cannot avoid needing, because a state does not survive torpor. Her notes are this technique's output and she has never once been able to check them.

The claim every Mind tradition rests and none can prove inside a mortal window is that the self being cultivated is separable from the one doing the cultivating. She is the one practitioner on the tier who cannot examine the claim at all, because for eleven months there is no self in her to examine and the claim is untestable by construction.

The gate where a practitioner holds a self and a body at once without one cancelling the other, and it is the gate most in question in her, since the continuity of her self is carried by a document held by somebody else and the body that is not here for eleven months of the year.

The fourth digest group opens for twelve meridians and the sea rises on it, and she clears gates out of accumulated reserve rather than on a chosen day, so her progress has never once arrived when she decided. She describes every advance she has made as late and none as forced.

A single-culture people for whom eleven months of torpor makes widowhood a normal state rather than a grief. They are the only population in the setting whose year and this species' year are the same, and they are the reason her absences are counted as a season rather than as a leaving.

A house that owns the ground on both sides of the only crossing of the Sixfold Ridge and grants passage rather than selling it, and this is the body that makes the grant safe: it reaches the pass, delivers and leaves before anyone has to decide whether it might stay. She declines their post every year anyway.

reference_stats.summary: A mind practitioner whose entire body of work is destroyed on a schedule and whose continuity is therefore carried by a book in somebody else's hand. Her species' accumulating qi makes breakthroughs late and rarely fail, and the eleven months she is not awake make all of it unreadable by the person who has to use it.
strengths: Qi accumulates in her rather than circulating, so her breakthroughs are late and rarely fail, and she has never wasted a reserve on an attempt she did not finish.
Holds her soul deep and quiet enough to be difficult to read and hard to damage, which is the single best defensive fact on the ridge and costs her nothing to keep.
Carries the ridge's habits rather than its orders, so a pass held by her is held by a practice and survives her being carried off it.
Can produce, from memory, the complete recorded state of a technique she has not performed in eleven months, because the record is not memory and never was.
Learns in eight weeks a year, which means she is a faster study than anyone with a full calendar and has been for most of her life.
weaknesses: Is slow and nearly helpless in torpor, and a hibernating longwinter is a large, warm, immobile target that cannot be woken quickly.
Cannot verify her own record, so her competence rests entirely on a document she wrote and cannot read until next spring and on other people's hands.
Lives in a season and a warm year is a bad year, so a decade of climate on this ridge would end her practice rather than slow it.
Cannot be woken quickly, which is the one thing a border-holder on the only crossing wants and cannot have.
Has lost her whole body of work once already, in a single week, and has no procedure for what to do about it except write it down again.
reference_stats.combat_read: There is nothing to outlast in her, because her qi accumulates and her breakthroughs rarely fail, and there is nothing in her worth reading at range because her soul is held deep and quiet. What ends her is arithmetic about the season: fight her in the eight weeks and she is faster than anyone who has had a full year, and fight her in the winter and she is a large warm immobile object with no art at all and no way to be woken. She will tell you which eight weeks those are.
notes: The pairing on this record is physiological and institutional rather than a rule the bible states. The lore authorises the eleven-month torpor, the lowered core, the accumulating qi and the flank-vessel wall; it does not state that her continuity must be carried externally, and that is this character's answer to her own species rather than an authored mechanic.

cultivation.bladder is not on this record and no meridian is written as a rung. Its authored tier is the body path's bookkeeping vessel and is a different axis from a ladder position, and the flank vessels are named here only as the two-gradient structure the lore uses to explain her ceiling.

The seventeenth gate is a season and not a discipline, and she says so in every telling. It is the arithmetic of one warm gradient against a requirement for two, arrived at annually, and no amount of practice alters it.

cultivation.passive_echo_resonance is the shaping record because the whole character is what happens when a technique's best remembered state has to outlive the body that found it, and because the setting's most reliable record of that state is a book kept by somebody who is not her.

art.palette_notes: Oiled brown and undyed wool, heavy and low contrast, with one bright green: the thresh cord knotted at the left wrist, the only chosen colour she owns and permitted in every frame. Continuity marker: the eleven shallow scars at the wrists, one per season she has come out of torpor somewhere other than where she went in, and the notebook on the chalk-cord belt. Skin reads ruddy in the eating weeks and greys visibly as she cools, and that change is allowed to happen across a series and is not a lighting change.
